<h2>Evaluate a Functional-Type Classification Change</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Compares two functional-type classifications by taxon, raw cluster
labels, label-invariant co-clustering relationships, and silhouette
widths. The partition comparison is invariant to arbitrary integer
relabelling of otherwise identical clusters.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_functional_type_classification_change(data_reference, data_candidate)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="data_reference">data_reference</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame with unique 'taxon_name' values and columns
'functional_type' and 'silhouette_width'.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="data_candidate">data_candidate</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame with the same required columns as 'data_reference'.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Label-invariant partition differences are counted from cluster-size
and contingency-table combinations. This avoids constructing a
quadratic taxon-by-taxon matrix while counting pairs that are in the
same cluster in exactly one classification.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>A named list with 'data_summary', a one-row tibble of comparison
counts, and 'data_taxon_comparison', a taxon-level full join of both
classifications.
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>data_reference &lt;- tibble::tibble(
  taxon_name = c("a", "b", "c"),
  functional_type = c(1L, 1L, 2L),
  silhouette_width = c(0.4, 0.5, 0.6)
)
data_candidate &lt;- tibble::tibble(
  taxon_name = c("a", "b", "c"),
  functional_type = c(2L, 2L, 1L),
  silhouette_width = c(0.4, 0.5, 0.6)
)
evaluate_functional_type_classification_change(
  data_reference,
  data_candidate
)
</code></pre>
